Harry James Bush (born August 20, 1989) is an English cricketer who is best known for his prolific scoring in university and club cricket. While he did not have a long-term professional career with a first-class county, he made a significant mark during his time in the MCC University system.

Here is everything you need to know about his career and achievements:

### 1. Personal Background
*   **Born:** August 20, 1989, in Wimbledon, London.
*   **Role:** All-rounder (Right-handed batsman and Right-arm medium-fast bowler).
*   **Education:** He attended Oxford Brookes University, which allowed him to play for the Oxford MCCU (Marylebone Cricket Club University) side.

### 2. First-Class Career
Bush played first-class cricket between 2010 and 2012. During this era, matches played by MCC University sides against professional county teams were granted official first-class status.

*   **Teams:** Oxford MCCU.
*   **Statistics:** In 7 first-class matches, he scored 380 runs at an impressive average of 31.66.
*   **The "Century Against the Pros":** His career highlight occurred in April 2012. Playing for Oxford MCCU against **Warwickshire** (who were the reigning County Champions or runners-up at the time), Bush scored a magnificent **114**. This innings was highly regarded because it came against a professional attack that included bowlers like Chris Wright and Jeetan Patel.

### 3. Playing Style
As a tall, upright batsman, Bush was known for his "correct" technique and ability to drive the ball well. As a bowler, he provided useful medium-pace, though his batting was clearly his primary strength at the first-class level.

### 4. County Involvement
While he never secured a full-time professional contract with a senior county, he was frequently involved in the professional circuit:
*   **Surrey CCC:** Bush played extensively for the Surrey Second XI. Although he performed well, the fierce competition for places in the Surrey middle order during that period made it difficult for him to break into the first team.
*   **Minor Counties:** He also represented **Suffolk** in the Minor Counties Championship, where he was a consistent performer.

### 5. Club Cricket Dominance
If Harry Bush is a legend anywhere, it is in the **Surrey Championship** (one of the strongest club leagues in England).
*   He has been a stalwart for **Wimbledon Cricket Club** for over a decade.
*   He is considered one of the most prolific batsmen in the history of the league, regularly scoring hundreds and helping Wimbledon win multiple Premier Division titles.
*   In the amateur/club circuit, he is often cited as a "pro in all but name," possessing a level of skill that many believe could have succeeded in the professional game had the right opportunities lined up at the right time.

### 6. Career Transition
Like many cricketers who excel at the University level but do not transition into a 15-year professional career, Bush moved into the professional world outside of playing. He has worked in the financial sector in London while continuing to dominate the club cricket scene on weekends.

### Summary of Stats (First-Class)
*   **Matches:** 7
*   **Innings:** 13
*   **Runs:** 380
*   **Highest Score:** 114
*   **Average:** 31.66
*   **100s/50s:** 1 / 1
*   **Wickets:** 4 (Best bowling 2/43)

Harry Bush serves as a prime example of the high quality of "uncontracted" cricket in England—players who have the talent to play at the highest level but primarily showcase their skills in the University and Premier Club systems.
